title: Build a balanced board
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Who sits around the table when your company's biggest decisions are made?

Jose said that, as entrepreneurs and in a company, the formation of a board of directors is necessary, because it is very scary for investors not to have a board set up. You want a balanced board. A typical board is five to seven members, always an uneven number, so that when you vote you don't get gridlocked between two groups.
A student said: a board member has to make unbiased decisions, but also has to be good politically.

Jose said: people have to see that you are surrounded by people who have experience in the industry. You want a managing director responsible for overseeing the whole business, executive directors who manage finance, sales and operations, and maybe a non-executive director.

The non-executive director might be someone who has been successful in the industry and gives strategic advice, he said. You generally also want a person who audits the financials and gives an opinion on financial reporting and internal processes.

A student who served on an industry group's board said: the important thing I took away is the diversity of opinions, thoughts, backgrounds and experience. What you don't want is a rubber-stamp board, people who accept a seat but aren't willing to challenge the chief executive or make the tough calls. The strength of the board determines the strength of the company.

Whenever I see a young entrepreneur starting a business, Jose said, the first thing they need is a board of advisors, who help them look at the right fundamentals. Board of advisors can be seen as mentors. Not having one is a bad sign.
Typically venture capital firms create the boards for the entrepreneur, he said, and it gets into the bylaws and the shareholders. The bylaws can be a hundred pages long or much shorter.
Who are your first three advisors, and what would each challenge in you?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the people who advise you now.
Write the board you would build: managing director, executives, one outsider, one who audits.
Write the odd number you would choose.
Write the first advisor you will ask.

check.q: Why did Jose say a board has an uneven number of members?
choices: Because it is the law everywhere

check.q: What did a student say you don't want?
What did Jose say a young entrepreneur needs first?

recap: Build a balanced board, or at least a board of advisors who will challenge you.
